extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants, GHG emissions attestation providers, and legal/compliance professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the SEC's final-rule criteria governing GHG emissions attestation providers, assurance levels, timing, independence, expertise, acceptable standards, and related disclosures for registrants subject to Items 1505/1506.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing, incorporation, and placement of attestation report
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant that elects to incorporate by reference its attestation report from its Form 10-Q for the second fiscal quarter or to provide its attestation report in an amended annual report must include an express statement in its annual report indicating its intention to either incorporate by reference the attestation report from a quarterly report on Form 10-Q or amend its annual report to provide the attestation report by the due date specified in Item 1505.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed requirement to include the attestation report in a separately captioned “Climate-Related Disclosure” section was not adopted; registrants may place the attestation report where they choose (other than financial statement disclosures) and may elect to use a separate caption. The rules provide an additional two fiscal quarters in some circumstances to measure emissions, obtain assurance, and prepare the attestation report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary assurance and applicable requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any voluntary assurance over any GHG emissions disclosure must comply with the disclosure requirements in Item 1506(e). Any voluntary assurance obtained over GHG emissions disclosures that are not required to be assured pursuant to Item 1506(a) must follow the requirements of Item 1506(b) through (d), including using the same attestation standard as the registrant's required assurance over Scope 1 and/or Scope 2 disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tabled distinctions: (a) After GHG disclosure compliance but before assurance compliance, voluntary assurance must meet Item 1506(e). (b) After assurance compliance date, voluntary assurances over non-required GHG items (e.g., voluntary Scope 3) must follow Items 1506(b)-(d) and use the same attestation standard as required assurance to avoid confusion. Registrants not subject to Items 1505/1506 still must comply with Item 1506(e) for any voluntary assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the assurance rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission narrowed the scope of the final rule to apply only to GHG emissions disclosures that are not required to be assured under Item 1506(a) and did not extend the assurance requirements to other climate-related disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This narrowing was intended to reduce complexity and reflects the Commission's view that registrants are unlikely to voluntarily obtain assurance over non-GHG climate disclosures for which Item 1506(e) disclosure would be useful to investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: GHG emissions attestation provider — expertise / significant experience
rubrics_metrics.description: A GHG emissions attestation provider must be an expert in GHG emissions by virtue of having significant experience in measuring, analyzing, reporting, or attesting to GHG emissions. Significant experience means having sufficient competence and capabilities necessary to: (a) perform engagements in accordance with professional standards and applicable legal and regulatory requirements; and (b) enable the service provider to issue reports that are appropriate under the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The expertise requirement applies to the person or firm signing the attestation report. If the service provider is a firm, the Commission would expect policies and procedures designed to provide reasonable assurance that personnel selected to conduct the engagement have significant experience with attestation engagements and GHG emissions; however, the final rules do not mandate specific policies or a minimum number of years of experience, favoring a principles-based, holistic assessment of qualifications rather than a rigid "years-of-experience" threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence requirement and determining factors
rubrics_metrics.description: A GHG emissions attestation provider must be independent with respect to the registrant, and any of its affiliates, for whom it is providing the attestation report, during the attestation and professional engagement period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modeled on Rule 2-01 of Regulation S-X, independence is assessed by whether a relationship or service creates a mutual/conflicting interest, places the provider in a position of attesting to its own work, results in the provider acting as management or an employee, or makes the provider an advocate for the registrant. All relevant circumstances—including financial or other relationships—are considered. Registrants and providers must comply with Item 1506 independence requirements, but are not separately required to comply with Rule 2-01 itself; existing Rule 2-01 guidance may nevertheless be a useful starting point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable attestation standards and quality control frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules require the use of attestation standards established by a body or group that has followed due process procedures. The Commission explicitly permits certain standards (including IAASB and ISO standards) and considered PCAOB/AICPA frameworks but did not require PCAOB registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission retained a principles-based approach permitting non-PCAOB and non-accounting firms to provide attestation if they use acceptable attestation standards. Commenters urged requiring accreditation (e.g., ISO 14065, ISO 14064-3) or PCAOB registration; the Commission declined to impose specific accreditation or PCAOB registration at this time but noted that additional minimum quality control requirements for providers not using PCAOB/AICPA/IAASB standards were considered and not adopted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written consent and securities-law liability of attestation providers
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant is required to obtain and include the written consent of the GHG emissions attestation provider pursuant to Securities Act section 7 and related rules. The GHG emissions attestation provider is subject to liability under the Federal securities laws for the attestation conclusion or, when applicable, opinion provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters supported amending Rule 436 to limit section 11 liability for limited assurance reports to encourage provider participation; others opposed limiting expertized status. The Commission recognized concerns that section 11 liability could deter providers but retained the consent and potential liability framework, noting liability should encourage due diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accreditation, additional qualifications, and Commission stance
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters recommended requiring membership in or accreditation by specific bodies (e.g., ISO 14065, ISO 14064-3, IAF members, ANAB) or PCAOB registration; some recommended staff oversight or a PCAOB process for climate-specific service providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission decided not to impose a specific accreditation or membership requirement given the evolving nature of GHG assurance and the potential emergence of new accreditation bodies. Instead, the Commission retained a principles-based set of expertise/attestation/independence requirements intended to ensure sufficient competence while preserving flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on attesting to provider's own preparatory work / conflict-of-interest rule
rubrics_metrics.description: An expert or third-party that has assisted a registrant in calculating or preparing its GHG emissions data would likely not meet the independence requirements because such an engagement would place the attestation provider in the position of attesting to its own work or creating a mutual interest with the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission views this conflict as precisely the situation the independence requirement is intended to prevent. Registrants that hire a preparer may need to pay both the preparer and an independent attestation provider. The phased-in compliance period is intended to reduce the likelihood of registrants needing to use conflicted providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: State licensure and non-CPA providers
rubrics_metrics.description: States typically require a party that holds itself out as a public accountant to be licensed as a CPA; non-CPAs are not able to use certain AICPA or PCAOB attestation standards that are restricted to CPAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, IAASB and ISO standards permitted under the final rules are not restricted to CPAs, and the Commission is not aware of state laws preventing non-CPA service providers from providing assurance over GHG emissions, so non-CPAs may perform attest services provided they are not holding themselves out as CPAs nor using CPA-only attestation standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firm policies and quality-control expectations (not mandated)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission stated it would expect a firm service provider to have policies and procedures designed to provide reasonable assurance that the personnel selected to conduct the GHG emissions attestation engagement have significant experience with attestation engagements and GHG emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although this expectation exists, the final rules do not mandate that firms adopt particular policies or procedures; the Commission declined to include a prescriptive requirement because it did not want to foreclose other means by which a firm may ensure that personnel meet the expertise requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phased-in compliance timeline and transition accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules provide phased-in compliance periods (including an additional two fiscal quarters in certain cases) before registrants are required to obtain attestation reports and include multi-year transition periods before assurance requirements fully apply to give registrants and providers time to comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The phased-in approach is intended to mitigate concerns about the supply and availability of qualified providers, allow non-accountant providers time to adapt to independence requirements, and give newly public companies (e.g., SRCs and EGCs) time before becoming subject to assurance requirements. During interim periods, certain limited disclosure requirements (e.g., Item 1506(e)) apply.
